sentences.text: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.
An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy and, paradoxically, higher confidence.
Researchers tested this by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence.
The method was verified by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex.
For both humans and monkeys, increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence.
This increase in noise affected the accuracy only subtly, and this was not statistically reliable, meaning accuracy was minimally impaired.
The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.
The results across species were explained by a common mechanism of bounded evidence accumulation.
The study shows how volatility in sensory evidence influences choice, reaction time, and confidence in a perceptual decision.

sentences.text: The Shigella flexneri enzyme OspI specifically targets a glutamine residue in UBC13 and converts it to glutamate (Q100E) through deamidation.
This deamidation of UBC13 by OspI silences the host's NF-κB inflammatory response.
The modification silences the polyubiquitination activity of the complex formed with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6.
Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and the TRAF6 RING-domain by perturbing both the native and transient interactions.
This inhibition occurs without perturbing the overall UBC13 structure or its intrinsic enzymatic activity.
Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
Specifically, E100 in dUBC13 competes with an intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge to form an internal salt-bridge.
Electrostatic repulsion between the newly formed glutamate (E100) and the negatively charged surface of the RING domain also prevents transient interactions.
This repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING further disrupts the UBC13/RING complex.
This study provides molecular details of how a post-translational modification can modulate transient protein-protein association to inhibit interaction.
The pathogen employs subtle mechanisms like salt-bridge competition and modification of transient complexes to block protein-protein association.

sentences.text: Synchronisation of oscillatory activity might contribute to working memory by enabling the coordination of long-range processes.
Researchers applied 6 Hz theta tACS to the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule nodes.
The stimulation was sinusoidal with a 6 Hz frequency and a peak-to-peak amplitude of 1000 μA.
Synchronous tACS improved reaction times for the more demanding 2-back condition compared both to desynchronous tACS and sham.
The synchronous tACS produced sufficient improvement in response times to make 2-back performance similar to the 1-back condition.
This stimulation increased activity within the inferior parietal lobe and middle frontal gyrus.
Increased activity within the right inferior parietal lobe correlated with faster responses during the 2-back task.
Synchronous stimulation resulted in increased functional connectivity between parietal and frontal areas.
Specifically, functional connectivity increased between the IPL-electrode region and frontal parts of the network, such as the DLPFC.

sentences.text: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.
Researchers used optogenetic circuit mapping in 70 mice to reveal parallel circuits in the superficial RSG that process disparate inputs.
The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum are sources of spatial information that strongly and selectively recruit small low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal cells in the RSG.
In contrast, neighboring regular-spiking (RS) cells are preferentially controlled by inputs from the claustrum and anterior cingulate.
These inputs from the claustrum and anterior cingulate are sources of mostly non-spatial information.
Computational models of LR neurons can compute the speed of head rotation using head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.
LR cells can conjunctively encode both head direction and head speed.
These parallel input streams identify LR neurons as a distinct principal neuronal subtype.
This subtype is ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG.

sentences.text: Flowers from genetically diverse Arabidopsis thaliana accessions consistently produce four petals.
This phenotype is robust to natural genetic variation in the Arabidopsis thaliana species.
In contrast, Cardamine hirsuta flowers display a variable number of petals, between zero and four, on a single plant.
The divergence in the pleiotropic floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness.
The Arabidopsis thaliana AP1 gene masks the phenotypic expression of all petal number quantitative trait loci (QTL) in Cardamine hirsuta.
This masking effect involves epistatic interactions that hide the phenotypic effects of at least 9 QTL.
The functional difference between the species mapped broadly to upstream regulatory regions rather than coding regions of AP1.
This means the way the AP1 gene is controlled, rather than the protein it makes, contributes to the divergence in petal number robustness.
By masking these QTL, the Arabidopsis thaliana version of the AP1 gene ensures a robust count of four petals.
The variable petal number in Cardamine hirsuta remains because its version of AP1 does not perform this masking function.

sentences.text: Sulforaphane (SFN) is a natural product found in cruciferous vegetables that activates the transcription regulator Nrf2.
SFN blocks HIV infection in primary human macrophages but does not block infection in primary T cells.
The depletion of Nrf2 using siRNA caused a significant increase in HIV infection levels in primary human macrophages.
These data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in these immune cells.
SFN treatment blocks infection after the virus enters the cell but before the formation of 2-LTR circles.
This impact occurs after reverse transcription has taken place.
The inhibition of HIV by SFN occurs even though known anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 were not upregulated.
Specifically, SFN does not block HIV by increasing SAMHD1 levels.
In contrast to Marburg, Dengue, and KSHV, which benefit from Nrf2, HIV is blocked through Nrf2 activation.
The discovery that Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages stands in contrast with other viruses.

sentences.text: In the Dominican Republic, the appearance of Zika virus cases closely followed a large dengue epidemic.
Data showed that 75% of dengue was reported in those aged <20 years, while the median age was ~42 for Zika.
Zika infections appeared to be highly clustered among females, who made up 73.8% of reported cases.
However, Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males at 0.62 per 10,000 population compared to 0.57 in females.
Evidence suggests little impact of existing dengue immunity on the reported attack rates of Zika at the population level.
Community awareness campaigns, through influencing short-term health-seeking behaviour, remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women of reproductive age.

sentences.text: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten vegetative cells.
Researchers studied this process using a chromosomally-encoded hetR-gfp fusion to track the transcription factor HetR.
The study found that expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled within a spatial range of two to three cells.
These correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.
The inhibitor PatS, the septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of these fluctuations.
The results show that cell-cell communication can control stochasticity in gene expression to create a developmental pattern.

sentences.text: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings ( dual-adaptation ) when feedback for each is provided alternately .
Participants performed a target-pointing task in which we manipulated the spatial mapping of the visual feedback .
Participants' task was to try and tap in the corresponding location on the graphics tablet as accurately and as quickly as possible within a 1 second time limit .
The target shapes were taken from a continuous set of shapes , morphed between spiky and circular shapes .
In this task , participants had to point more to the right in order to hit spiky target shapes and more to the left to hit the round ones .
The results showed that participants apply the mapping corresponding to the trained shape that is most similar to the current one .
This behavior is consistent with a Bayesian learning model where the mapping for the more extreme shapes is the same as for the nearest trained shape .
The study also found that learning should slow down with increased numbers of training pairs .
Specifically , learning the shape-mapping contingencies seemed to be much harder in the 5-Pair Condition than in the 2-Pair Condition .

sentences.text: Many countries cannot start or expand neglected tropical disease programs because they lack necessary baseline data.
Researchers developed and field-tested an integrated mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
The specific purpose of the ITM protocol is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions has been attained.
The protocol was tested by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
However, the ITM methodology resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis.
The ITM protocol was feasible and resulted in a 31% overall cost saving in Mali and a 19% overall cost saving in Senegal compared to standard WHO methodologies.
